messages:
incident-bot: Pager: [P1] metering-service token-count drift detected — token_count delta ~+17% vs baseline over last 30m. Auto-escalation to #incidents and oncall. Incident page: https://ops.redwood/incident/1765123456

alice.ng: Ack, oncall taking. Starting quick triage — pinging billing and infra.

ben.s: @alice.ng oncall here. Any customer-facing alerts firing?

billing-eng: seeing spike in `overage_flags` for window 2026-03-17T14:00Z -> 14:15Z. Affected ~12 customers flagged. Values look higher than token telemetry by ~10-20%.

carla-m: copying query I ran (short):
```sql
SELECT window_start, SUM(tokens) as tokens_sum, SUM(emitter_count) as emitter_sum
FROM metering.agg_15m
WHERE window_start >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY window_start
ORDER BY window_start DESC;
```

carla-m: results: latest window: tokens_sum=1,227,450, emitter_sum=1,010,300 (expected ~1.1M) — suggests token counter ahead of emitter counts.

alice.ng: noted. This looks like a token counting drift (producer side increment) rather than pure ingestion lag. Checking producer logs and kafka offsets.

oncall-sre: kafka consumer lags: 0 for metering-consumer. Producer logs show occasional duplicate ack retries for EmitterService between 14:03-14:07. Pasting snippet:
```
2026-03-17T14:04:12Z EmitterService WARN duplicate write attempt id=abc123 (retries=3)
2026-03-17T14:04:13Z EmitterService INFO send ok id=abc123
```

ben.s: duplicates -> likely double-counting at write stage. Can we identify if the write path increments token_count before idempotency check?

carla-m: yes, there's a window where producer increments counter pre-commit. Deploy change last week had a small race under retry. Rolling back the producer hotfix might revert to idempotent path.

billing-eng: customers flagged: (redacted list) — volume users first. We should mute automated overage emails to avoid false alarms while we triage.

alice.ng: Agreed. @billing-eng please mute alerting for the affected windows and annotate incident page. I will open a short-lived blocker to disable alert rule for `overage_flags > 1` for 30m.

billing-eng: done — alerting muted for rule `billing.overage_flags.v1` until 14:45Z. Adding note: "muted due to tokencount drift investigation" :white_check_mark:

jordan: Support notification drafted, recommend Tier 1 copy: "We’re investigating elevated usage flags; if you received an overage email in the last 30 minutes it may be spurious. We will follow up by EOD with reconciliation." Want approval to send now?

pm-ops: Send now with wording above, call out mitigation steps and ETA for reconciliation.

alice.ng: go ahead, send. Also start reprocess of recent 30m windows to produce corrected counts (idempotent path). Command I kicked off:
```
./infra/reprocess-meting-windows --from 2026-03-17T13:45Z --to 2026-03-17T14:15Z --mode=idempotent --parallel=4
```

alice.ng: reprocess started, tracking job id reproc-1765123456-1.

ben.s: what's ETA on reprocess?

alice.ng: estimate ~18 minutes for the 30m window. Will watch for job completion and reconcile emitter vs token counts.

carla-m: quick reconciliation query I will run after job completes to confirm fix:
```sql
SELECT window_start,
  SUM(tokens) as tokens_after,
  SUM(emitter_count) as emitter_after
FROM metering.agg_15m_reprocessed
WHERE window_start BETWEEN '2026-03-17T13:45:00Z' AND '2026-03-17T14:15:00Z'
GROUP BY window_start;
```

billing-eng: after initial reprocess results (partial): latest window tokens_after=1,012,980, emitter_after=1,010,450 — much closer. Overage flags dropped from 12 -> 1 (likely a genuine high-usage customer).

ben.s: good. Can we unmute alerts for non-affected windows? We should keep muted only for the specific window set.

billing-eng: unmuted global rule; recreated a scoped mute for windows 14:00-14:15 only. Alerts will resume for others.

pm-ops: Support notified customers flagged earlier; ticket created REQ-4892 for manual reconciliation for the one remaining flagged customer.

oncall-sre: I'm going to stay on this until reprocess completes and hand off to @ben.s for watch. If anything spikes, add `pager` tag.

alice.ng: reprocess finished. Final reconciliation shows token vs emitter delta within 0.2% for all windows. Overages reconciled except REQ-4892.

carla-m: root cause: producer hotfix introduced non-idempotent increment on retry path. Filed PR rollback: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4521. Will schedule emergency rollback to canary now.

ben.s: rolling back canary to previous image (image: v2.8.4 -> v2.8.3) in us-east-1. Command: `kubectl set image deploy/emitter emitter=repo/emitter:v2.8.3 -n prod-us-east`

alice.ng: rollback confirmed in canary; no new duplicate writes observed in logs for 10m.

billing-eng: closing incident alert on billing side. Will run nightly backfill to ensure historical exports unaffected.

pm-ops: drafting post-incident note for customers impacted and internal postmortem. Assigning follow-ups: 
- carla-m: revert hotfix and add integration test for retry idempotency
- billing-eng: run full backfill and produce reconciliation report by EOD
- alice.ng / ben.s: validate metrics pipeline and add monitor for producer duplicate-audit

oncall-sre: Handoff: @ben.s taking follow-up watch for next 8 hours. I’ll update rotation calendar. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 

ben.s: taking handoff. Will watch for regressions and confirm PR rollback CI tomorrow morning.

alice.ng: incident closed for live mitigation. Postmortem draft requested in #postmortems by EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident 1765123456 status -> resolved (mitigation complete). Timeline and notes saved to https://ops.redwood/incident/1765123456/notes
